newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower amid softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower amid softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open lower Monday amid early talk of softer Gulf cash prices, industry sources said.
May, which is set to expire this Thursday, ranged from $2.05 to $2.065 in over-the-counter trade after settling to the upside Friday at $2.081 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked two to three cents lower at $2.05-2.09 per mmBtu.

Traders said support in May was pegged at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825. If the contract moves higher on the impending cooler weather, the next obstacle will be $2.095, traders said, adding further resistance was at $2.16 and $2.21-2.23.

In Friday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents to about $2.05. Midcontinent pipes also were up slightly to the low-to-mid $1.90s. Weekend gas at the New York city gate fell about five cents to about $2.40.

Cooler-than-normal weather is forecast to continue through this week in the Northeast and Midwest, with temperatures about five to 10 degrees below normal expected to blanket the southern plains and Texas. Normal to slightly above-normal temperatures are forecast for the Southeast and Northwest.
